newsitem.title: UK: British shipping industry to focus on port control.
newsitem.headline: British shipping industry to focus on port control.

text.p: The British Chamber of Shipping (COS), which represents about 90 percent of the UK shipping industry, will seek to further European port state controls, according to its new president.
Paul Skinner said today at the COS annual general meeting: "During my presidency, the Chamber will do all that it can to encourage more consistent port state control measures."

Skinner, who took over today as head of the COS from outgoing president Anthony Cooke, said there was a need for the COS to address its contacts with the European Commission to make sure that all ports followed the same procedures.
"It is ironic that there is strong evidence that Europe is one of the areas of the world to which poor quality ships come when port state controls are made more effective elsewhere," he said.
"Europe, as the home of the port state control initiative must do more to ensure that it is a hostile environment for the substandard ship."
Skinner added that competitiveness and quality -- in terms of safety and the environment -- were also issues British shipping needs to address.
As a director with Shell International Petroleum Company, he said the group had discovered it could improve its competitiveness by "benchmarking" its shipping operations against leading competitors.
"I am convinced that we all have much to learn from each other," he said.
"Environmental issues are also part of building a superior image for British shipping which makes it a product people want to buy," he added. -- Paul Berrill Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087
